Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity MAP — HelixAI evaluation & GPU pool scaling contingency

Hi Sana —

Thanks again for the time last week. Attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that aligns the evaluation milestones with the capacity reservation windows we'll need to hit production SLAs if you decide to reserve Dedicated capacity. Key asks:

- Confirm Helix's preferred evaluation cadence (2-week vs 4-week sprint).
- Confirm target go-live window (earliest/target/latest).
- Flag any procurement constraints (PO timing, internal approvals).

Highlights from the draft (see HelixAI_MAP_v1.xlsx attached):
- Recommended GPU pool: 32 A100-equivalent GPUs initially (supports 80 rps sustained with 1.5k token average).
- Tranche approach: 50% initial commit for evaluation-to-staging, 50% follow-on after acceptance testing (reduces lead-time exposure).
- Procurement lead time assumptions: 8–12 weeks for dedicated pool reservation in our default (non-burst) regions; 4–6 weeks for burst/spot-enabled top-up.

We also included a contingency plan if hardware lead times slip: temporary transient routing to hosted variants + KV-prefix caching configuration to keep latency targets while you lock in capacity.

Next steps proposal: if you can confirm the evaluation sprint length and any internal procurement windows by EOD Friday, Vanessa and I will lock the MAP and draft a DocuSign-ready terms packet.

Cheers,
Sergio
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: HelixAI_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_dedicated_terms_v2.pdf

From: Sana Patel <sana@helixai.com>

Cc: Leo Martin <leo@helixai.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@helixai.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity MAP — HelixAI evaluation & GPU pool scaling contingency

Sergio —

Appreciate the thorough MAP. Quick answers from my side:

- Evaluation cadence: 3-week sprints (we prefer a slightly longer loop to fully exercise data pipelines).
- Target go-live window: earliest mid-July, target end of July, latest mid-August (tight but budgeted).
- Procurement: PO approvals take ~6 weeks (internal legal + finance), but we can expedite to 3 weeks with an approved term sheet.

A couple of clarifying questions:
1) Can you break down the 32-GPU recommendation into model-specific capacity? We plan to run two families concurrently (chat-generation and embeddings).
2) If we do the 50/50 tranche approach, what's the billing/pricing cadence (monthly vs committed upfront)?

If you can get me a short appendix on model-split sizing and billing cadence, I can present to finance next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Sana Patel
Head of Platform, HelixAI
sana@helixai.com

Sana / Sergio —

Quick sizing appendix as requested (summary here; I'll attach a one-pager into the Drive link):

- Assumptions: chat model ~6 tokens/response avg, tail latency target 500ms; embeddings jobs batched, throughput target 400 qps.
- Suggested split of 32 GPUs: 22 GPUs for chat family (higher memory + KV use), 10 GPUs for embeddings (higher batch throughput).
- Alternative conservative start: 24 GPUs (16 chat / 8 embeddings) as an initial tranche to lower burn—then ramp to 32 after acceptance.

Procurement & billing notes:
- Tranche billing: committed capacity billed monthly against the reserved commitment. Up-front prepay optional for a discount; standard is monthly invoice.
- Overages: bursts beyond reserved pool are billed as on-demand at a premium rate unless you enable burst-capacity in the contract.
- Contract cadence: we can draft terms for a 12-month commitment with quarterly checkpoints.

I'll upload a concise model-split PDF to the Drive link and include a quick example cost table (likely helpful for finance).

-Vanessa
Director, Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Vanessa / Sergio —

Thanks for the breakdown. Finance/Procurement reviewed the tranche proposal and we can commit to the conservative start (24 GPUs) with the expectation to ramp to 32 GPUs after acceptance testing. Two procurement items:

1) We need a redline-ready term sheet (pricing + cancellation & SLA language). Please provide a DocuSign-ready packet we can circulate internally.
2) Lead time risk: if the 8–12 week reserve timeframe slips, can Redwood provide a temporary hosted fallback and a credit to offset any overage for the interim? We'd like the fallback documented in the MAP.

If you can get the packet and the fallback clause by Thursday this week, we can start the internal PO approvals loop and target a signed term sheet by Apr 30.

Regards,
